newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via overnight system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to add reserves to the banking system on Wednesday via overnight system repurchase agreements.
Analysts said that the Fed faces about a $15.5 billion a day add need in the two-week period that ends this session. But, only $7.9 billion of RPs are outstanding, they noted.
On Monday, the Fed added $8.65 billion in reserves, followed by $4.9 billion on Tuesday -- both through overnight system RPs.

Marc Wanshel, economist at J.P. Morgan & Co, pointed out that on the final day of the maintenance period, the Fed has provided a "genourous oversupply of reserves ... to minimize the risk of tight closes."
In the current period, federal funds have been tight, with fund trading above 6.0 percent on some days.
Early Wednesday, funds were at 5-15/16 percent, well above the 5-1/2 percent target rate.
"With the Fed effective well above the target, we think the (Open Market) Desk will be especially anxious to avoid a tight close tonight," Wanshel said.
